title: brakeman (first real run in a month) reports 2 medium SendFile warnings on the public media endpoint
evidence:
First real brakeman verdict in at least a month (the scan had never run -- see the brakeman commit: bin/brakeman --ensure-latest exited before scanning). It reports 2 medium-confidence SendFile warnings, "Model attribute used in file name", in app/controllers/media_controller.rb -- the photo action (send_file ... servable_file_path, ~line 43) and the reel action (reel_path, ~line 75) -- plus a weak EOLRails notice (Rails 8.0.4 support ends 2026-11-07).

DECIDED: accept, with the reasoning recorded, rather than change a live serving path. Basis, all verified in the file: params[:id] is an integer primary key (`ContentPillars::Photo.find(params[:id])`), so the file name is not attacker-shaped; the path is a DB column written by our own render pipeline, not user input; the endpoint additionally refuses to serve a photo no post references (the 2026-09-23 withhold rule), which is what closed the public-enumeration concern; and this endpoint IS the publisher's public media URL, so a blind containment check that resolves the wrong root would break publishing.

Mitigation if provenance ever changes (e.g. a user- or upload-supplied path): a root-containment check on File.expand_path plus a request spec. The scan is live from now on, so any such change re-surfaces this warning rather than hiding in a dark CI job.
